newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ back month bill futures close sharply stronger.
newsitem.headline: NZ back month bill futures close sharply stronger.

text.p: New Zealand bank bill futures in the back months -- September and December -- rose 12-13 points on hefty volume by the close on Wednesday.

Dealers were unsure whether the buying was related to the March futures closeout this morning or players taking positions ahead of Thursday's crucial six monthly economic forecasts by the Reserve Bank.
Whatever, the mood of the market, particularly in the short-end, was positive and the market expects the RB to take a relatively benign stance.
"With conditions as tight as they are, it's difficult to see why they would tighten further," an Auckland dealer said.
He said a further turn of the screws would see the Kiwi ratchet up, something neither politicians nor the bank wanted.
Another dealer said conditions were already considerably tighter than what the market predicts the bank will assume on Thursday.
The yield curve steepened as something of a squeeze was put on the short-dated bonds while the longer maturities proved more sticky.

Dealers said there was little interest in the testimony of Treasurer Winston Peters to the Finance and Expenditure Committee or that he was referred to the Privileges Committee following his fracas last week with a backbencher.
"Who cares. No one in the market believes what he says," said one dealer.
Another said Peters lacked credibility and the market would listen to what the RB said on Thursday.
